messages.subject: Automated porting of local GNU R libraries
messages.subject_clean: Automated porting of local GNU R libraries
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have just started using Renjin and I want to use some of my local R libraries in Renjin. I still want to use the library in GNU R too. So only maintaining one version of the library.

Is it possible for Renjin to share any experiences that they have with porting libraries into Renjin compatible form?

At the moment, I'm considering creating a gradle project that can support installing the library to local GNU R and to local maven for usage in Renjin.

I have also started a question on stackoverflow:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/39333462/automated-porting-of-r-library-for-renjin

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

I answered your question on StackOverflow: http://stackoverflow.com/a/39342577/3660721. This explains how you can use a single Maven POM file to compile a GNU R package for Renjin. You will need to automate the build yourself, for example using a bash script or something similar.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan

Thanks Maarten-Jan,

I've used your pom.xml in my project: https://github.com/micheal-swiggs/renjin-builder.

At the moment, there are commands to create a new renjin project that can be deployed as both a GNU R library & maven package that can be used in a renjin project.

Still a work in progress!

Micheal

We'll announce the availability of the new plugin here or in our monthly newsletter (sign up via http://www.renjin.org).

Regards,

Maarten-Jan

messages.subject: Re: optimize() function question.
messages.body_plain:
Hi 퇴깽스,

Renjin uses an implementation <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/c724b7b2ef7abfa45fb0d57796dd11177a7973fd/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/stats/internals/optimize/Optimizations.java#L265-L265> of Brent's algorithm from the Apache Commons Math library that was developed independently from GNU R's algorithm, so I'm not surprised there are differences in the intermediate steps, but both implementations (GNU R and Renjin) converge at a number approaching 9.0, which is the true minimum for this function in the domain [9, 10].

It's true that GNU R's error is lower than that of Renjin:

> f(9.000066) < f(9.00022655192689)
[1] TRUE

If this difference affects your analysis, please open an issue at https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin. We can look at compiling the C coded used by R to JVM bytecode to obtain exactly the same results as GNU R.

Best,
Alex
